messages:
acme-sre: Hey support — heads up, after we upgraded our plan and the invoice cleared at ~2026-03-05T00:03:10Z our org owner UI shows the +50k monthly tokens, but all requests from our service accounts keep getting 429 (quota exhausted).
acme-sre: Example curl + headers we see: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-service-XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: req_0abc1234
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Limit: 500000
X-Quota-Reset: 1768004400
X-Edge-Region: eu-west-1
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "message": "monthly bucket exhausted for key"
}
```
acme-sre: Notably the owner user key works ok from the UI (no 429). Service keys that were created before the upgrade are the ones failing. Any quick ideas?
support_lead: Thanks — can you paste org id and that request id (req_0abc1234)? Also which service key IDs are failing (just the prefix is fine).
acme-sre: Org: org-acme-55, request id: req_0abc1234, service keys affected: sk-service-XXXX, sk-service-YYYY
billing_engineer: I can confirm payment/top-up recorded in billing table at 2026-03-05T00:03:12Z for org-acme-55 (+50k tokens). Billing->ledger shows credit applied to org-level bucket.
platform_oncall: Checking quota allocation: we have two relevant systems — billing DB (authoritative credits) and edge per-key caches (fast lookup). Edge caches are per-API-key and have a 60s TTL.
platform_oncall: Hypothesis: the owner key triggers an immediate local cache invalidation (UI flow), but legacy service keys created before the upgrade missed the callback that flushes per-key caches, so edges still returned earlier cached zero balance until their TTL expired — but your X-Quota-Reset header points to 1768004400 which is only ~80s after the top-up.
platform_oncall: However, looking at audit logs I also see these service keys are under the legacy token mapping namespace (created prior to 2025-09-01 migration). The upgrade webhook we call for immediate sync didn't run for legacy-token keys due to an edge-case filter.
support_lead: Can we run a targeted sync for org-acme-55 and flush the edge cache in eu-west-1 for the affected key prefixes? We'll need acme-sre consent to touch service keys.
acme-sre: Please go ahead, we can tolerate a brief resync window.
platform_oncall: Ok running sync job: `scripts/sync_quota_by_org --org org-acme-55 --force-legacy` (will reconcile billing -> allocation table) and then `edgectl purge --region eu-west-1 --key-prefix sk-service-`
deploy-bot: job-7890: started sync_quota_by_org for org-acme-55 by platform_oncall
platform_oncall: Sync finished, allocation table shows monthly bucket now split and per-key allocations updated. Edge purge issued to eu-west-1; TTLs cleared.
support_lead: We also patched the filter to include legacy mappings so future upgrade/top-up flows will trigger the callback. Patch will be rolled into next deploy (canary now).
acme-sre: Confirmed — retries from our side now succeed, no 429s. Thanks for the quick turnaround :tada:
deploy-bot: job-7890: completed successfully (duration 18s)
platform_oncall: Root cause summary: top-up applied in billing DB but a subset of pre-migration service keys didn't receive the immediate cache-invalidation callback due to a filter bug. Visible effect: service keys returned cached zero balance at the edge until explicit purge or TTL expiry. Remediation: forced sync + edge purge; long-term: webhook filter fix and observability alert when an org top-up occurs but per-key allocation updates are below threshold.
support_lead: Action items assigned: billing_engineer to add a reconciliation check (alert if allocations != billing after top-up), platform_oncall to include legacy mapping in callback and add a short-term metric for per-key allocation lag.
acme-sre: appreciate it — leaving here in case others hit similar issue.
